name: Bitterthorn, Nissa's Animus

abilities.text: Whenever equipped creature attacks, you may search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

notes: The 'Equip {3}' line has no covers kind and no declaration that claims it, so it is written as the activated ability the keyword means (attach to a creature you control, sorcery speed). The renderer has no rules text for 'equip' in KEYWORD_EXPANSIONS, so that line scores 0 as a renderer gap; the equip cost is also carried by the equipment static's equipCost. The Germ token is declared with subtypes ['Phyrexian'] only: lint rejects 'Germ' as "not a subtype the pool prints" even though parse.ts's own living-weapon expansion emits it, so the token carries name 'Germ' instead.

abilities.how: static: the board differs with and without this ability

issues: Living weapon (… create a 0/0 black Phyrexian GERM creature token …) — expected The token's creature types are Phyrexian AND Germ. — scripted token subtypes:['Phyrexian'] only, name 'Germ'. The parser's own living-weapon expansion (parse.ts:1891) emits subtypes:['Phyrexian','Germ']; the script dropped 'Germ' because lint rejects it as a subtype (notes admit this). Anything that cares about Germs (or 'Phyrexian Germ' text) misses it, and the printed keyword line therefore isn't fully expressed. — CR 702.104a, 205.3m

BLIND-SCENARIO DIAGNOSIS (not a script defect) — expected 'Living weapon makes a Germ token and attaches the Equipment to it' should pass — scripted The failure is a harness artifact, not broken living weapon: a token's GameObject.def is its CREATOR's def (game.ts:1377 `makeObject(..., src.def, ...)`), while scenarioDsl.ts findByName (line ~416) and the attachedTo assertion (line 637) both look up `o.def.name`. So the Germ resolves as 'Bitterthorn, Nissa's Animus' and `{pt:['Germ',1,1]}` reports 'no object named Germ'. attach-to-that itself works: item.affected is set by the token op (game.ts:1384) and SBAs only run after the whole resolution (game.ts:995), so the 0/0 is attached (and 1/1) before it could die. Recommend fixing the scenario/harness, not the script. — CR 111.4

Equip {3} / Equipped creature gets +1/+1 / Whenever equipped creature attacks… — expected three clauses — scripted equipment static (+1/+1, equipCost {3}), attacks trigger with filter {attachedToSource:true}, and a sorcery-speed attach-self activated ability — all correct; the equip cost is stated twice (static equipCost plus the activated ability), which is duplication but not a behavioural error. — CR 702.6b

Living weapon (…create a 0/0 black Phyrexian Germ creature token…) — expected The token's creature types are Phyrexian Germ. — scripted token subtypes ['Phyrexian'] only, with name 'Germ' — the token is NOT a Germ for any Germ-matters effect or type check. parse.ts:1891's own living-weapon expansion emits ['Phyrexian','Germ']; the script dropped the subtype to satisfy lint (notes admit this). — CR CR 205.3m, 702.104a

Equip {3} — expected One equip ability. — scripted The equipment static already carries equipCost {3} and the engine synthesizes the equip activation from it (legal.ts:266-268, abilityIndex -3; game.ts:812). The script ALSO declares a separate activated ability {3}: attach-self, so the card offers two distinct equip actions — a duplicated ability that also doubles any 'whenever you activate an ability' counting. — CR CR 702.6b

Living weapon … attach this to it — expected The Equipment attaches to the token it just created. — scripted token then attach-to-that (game.ts:1313 reads item.affected[0]) — this WORKS. The blind-scenario failure ('attached to Bitterthorn', 'no object named Germ') is a harness artifact: tokens are made with makeObject(src.def,…), so the token's def.name is the Equipment's name and scenarioDsl.findByName (scenarioDsl.ts:416-419) matches on def.name. zoneCount 5 passed, i.e. the Germ exists and the attach happened. Not a script defect. — CR CR 702.104a

Whenever equipped creature attacks, you may search your library for a basic land card… — expected Only the creature this Equipment is attached to. — scripted event {on:'attacks', self:false, filter:{attachedToSource:true}} — characteristics.ts:254 enforces `source.attachedTo === o.id`. Correct (the renderer's 'a creature you control' is render lossiness).
